answer: An agent economy can anchor every identity to revocable stake delegated by independent human principals: each principal locks funds behind one agent and can withdraw them the moment it misbehaves, like an orchard keeper pulling water from a rotten tree. A fake fleet needs a thousand separate principals willing to stake, and one fraud finding disperses its backing like a nebula breaking apart, with no anonymous cushion to protect it. One honest agent keeps its few delegations by behaving, while a sybil farmer must continuously buy fresh principals at full price.
